data.name: Haimavathi
data.gender_notes: Haimavathi is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Haimavathi originated from the Sanskrit language and is derived from the words 'Haima' which means snow and 'Vathi' which means river. Haimavathi is the name of the Goddess of the snow-covered mountains. She is also known as Hemavathi, Haimavati or Haimavat. In Hindu mythology, Haimavathi is considered to be the wife of the sage Gautama and is the mother of the sage Parashurama.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of inner peace and tranquility.
data.etymology: Haimavathi belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Goddess of the Snow Mountains.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Haimavathi total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.
